The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by R.Jagannatha vs Narayanappa on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50210874/
1 him, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 23.06.2020 at about 6.30 pm., when he was going towards Malur from Kolar town with a load of vegetables in an Goods Auto Rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-08-9728 to transport vegetables and fruits from APMC yard Kolar to Malur town on hire basis at that time, near Chowdadenahalli village,
Kolar Taluk and district the driver of the auto rickshaw driven the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and capsized the auto rickshaw.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grevious head injuries.
Immediately he was taken to NIMHANS Bangalore.
The petitioner was doing vegetable business in wholesale and retail and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
After the accident, till today the SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.2619/2020 petitioner is completely bed ridden and lost his earnings.
The accident occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by its driver.
The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being its insurer are jointly and severally are liable to pay the compensation.
3. After service of summons, the respondents have appeared before the court and only Respondent No.2 has appeared through his counsel and filed the objections to main petition.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Respondent has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy to the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-9728 and the liability if any, shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the petitioner has to put strict proof of the same.
SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.2619/2020 Further contended that, the Mahindra Alfa Goods vehicle reg.No.KA-08-9728 did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and the FIR came to be lodged on 05.08.2020 i.e., after 42 days of the accident and the petitioner sustained injuries due to self-accident.
The driver of the alleged offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was returning in Goods Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-08-9728 on 23.06.2020 about 6.30 pm., near R.Jagannatha vs Narayanappa on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50210874/
2 Chowdadevanahalli village, Kolar Taluk and District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of same goods auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-08-9728 ?
SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.2619/2020 2.
What compensation petitioner is entitled ?
3. What Order ?
5. The petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.17.
He has also examined his witnesses Dr.Shailesh A V Rao as PW.2 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.P.18 to Ex.P.21.
On the other hand, on behalf of the respondent No.2 its Senior Legal Manager is examined as RW.1 and got one document as Ex.R.1 and closed their side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire records.

11. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, seizure panchanama, IMV report, wound certificate, final report, discharge summary,
medical bills etc., and got them marked at Ex.P.2, 3, 5, 6, 8 to 10, 12 and 17.
12.
I have perused Ex.P.2, 3, 5, 6, 8 to 10, 12 and 17.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 23.06.2020 at about 6.30 p.m.
and the FIR at Ex.P.2 in crime No.0276/2020 came to be registered on 05.08.2020 at around 13.30,
at Kolar Rural Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex . P.3
- complaint was lodged by wife of petitioner on 05.08.2020,
Ex. P.5 - spot panchanama reveals that on accident on 23.06.2020 at about 6.30 pm., on Kolar - Malur Tamber road, Chowdenahalli village gate.
The IMV SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.2619/2020 report marked at Ex.P.8 reveals that at the time of inspection no fresh damages found on the motor vehicle.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.10 against the driver of the offending Goods Auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-08-9728 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
13.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1.
In his cross-examination PW.1 denied that the injury sustained by him due to fall from somewhere else.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.2619/2020 dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore,
on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the offending Goods Autorickshaw which belongs to the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

14. ISSUE NO.2:
AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME: PW.1 has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.13.
As per this document, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 05.10.1956.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was aged about 64 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '7'.
15.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to accident, he was doing vegetable business in wholesale and retail and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Except oral suggestion he has not produced any document to show his avocation and actual income.
Even he has not adduced evidence of any witnesses in this regard.

sentences.text: As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.14,500/- as the accident took place in the year 2020.

16. PW.1 has deposed that after the accident he was taken to SNR Hospital, Kolar after first aid treatment he was taken to NIMHANS, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient for 2 days.
After that he took treatment as an inpatient for one week at Government Hospital, Malur on the advise given by NIMHANS.
As per Ex.P.9 - wound certificate, petitioner sustained sutured lacerated wound over right zygomatic region and CT brain plain shows left temporal hematoma with edema.
Doctor opines that the above injury is grevious in nature.
Petitioner has produced his discharge summary at Ex.P.12 of NIMHANS wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 24.06.2020 to 25.06.2020.
Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for total period of 2 days.
The petitioner in order to show his disability has examined Dr.Shailesh A V Rao as PW.2.

He has filed affidavit for his examination in chief and deposed that petitioner sustained injury to his head and was admitted to NIMHANS on 24.06.2020, CT brain revealed left temporal contusion with edema.
On 25.06.2020 he underwent left temporal craniotomy and evacuation of contusion and discharged on 25.06.2020, subsequently he was reportedly treated at Government Hospital, Malur.
On examination it revealed that a conscious patient with a left temporal scar, he had impaired memory and intelligence, he had poor verbal output and was unable to name simple objects.
MMSE was done on 23.01.2024 and he obtained a score of 17/30 which is low, skull X-ray done on 19.01.2024 revealed features of left fronto temporo parietal craniotomy, bone flap seen in situ.
PW.2 assessed whole body disability at 15%.

PW.2 has produced outpatient record, mini mental state examination, X-ray reports and bill receipt which are marked at Ex.P.18 to Ex.P.21.
18.
During cross examination he has admitted SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.2619/2020 that,

sentences.text: It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability, but the documents placed on record shows that he has the physical disability at 15% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 10% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
20. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-2 to disbelieve his version.
21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner has undergone pain SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.2619/2020 and sufferings to some extent.
Thus, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 2 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.29,000/- (14,500/- x 2) under this head.
23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
As already stated supra the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for nearly 2 days as it could be seen from Ex.P.12.
It is relevant to note that the petitioner has not produced documents to show that he took follow-up treatment.
Therefore, this tribunal inclines to award Rs.2,000/- under this head.
24. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 and 15 - tax invoice receipt,
Ex.p.16 - SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.2619/2020 2 bill receipt and Ex.P.17 - 2 medical bills.
Though Insurance Company disputed the medical expenses, nothing has been elicited during cross examination.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .9,008/- towards Medical Expenses.

. 
25. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '7'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m.
Hence, a sum of Rs.1,21,800/- (Rs.14,500 X 12 X 7 X 10/100) is awarded under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

R.Jagannatha vs Narayanappa on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50210874/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.

The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Pain and sufferings 25,000=00 2 Loss of income during 29,000=00 laid-up period 3

Attendant charges, extra 2,000=00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Medical expenses 9,008=00 5 Loss of future income due 1,21,800=00 to disability 6 Loss of future amenities & 25,000=00 happiness TOTAL Rs. 2,11,808=00
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,11,808/-.
28. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

29. LIABILITY:- In the absence of challenging the same, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Goods Auto Rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-08-9728 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.2619/2020 petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
The primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly,I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
30. ISSUE NO.3:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following :-
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,11,808/- (Rupees Two lakhs Eleven thousand Eight hundred Eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Goods Auto Rickshaw is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After the deposit of entire compensation amount, entire compensation shall be SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.2619/2020 released in favour of petitioner through E-payment upon proper verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
